identity.title: 3D-genome impacts of TAD-boundary-disrupting ultra-rare structural variants identified in schizophrenia.

content.abstract: Schizophrenia is a complex and multifactorial brain disorder that impacts ~1% of the U.S. population. The genetic architecture of schizophrenia includes 10 large rare structural variants (SVs) ~10 exonic variants, and over 250 common variants. Previously we combined whole genome sequencing (WGS) with brain-specific epigenomic data and found an excess of ultrarare SVs in schizophrenia localizing to the boundaries of topologically associated domains (TADs). Alterations in TAD boundaries (TAD-b) may lead to disarrangement of enhancer-promoter contacts and dysregulation of gene expression and have been associated with several human diseases. Our study sought to functionally characterize two of these TAD-b SVs using chromatin conformation capture (e.g., Hi-C) and RNA sequencing, to unveil mechanistic insight into the effects of these variants on 3D-genome organization and gene expression. To achieve this, we genetically engineered these two TAD-b SVs in isogenic induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) using CRISPR/Cas9. iPSCs were differentiated into neuronal precursor cells, excitatory glutamatergic neurons, and medium spiny neurons. We found that these TAD-boundary-disrupting SVs could reshape the 3D-genome and transcriptional networks in a cell-type-specific manner.
